evidence.claim: Cached evidence: U.S. Census reported April 2026 advance retail and food services sales of $757.1 billion, up 0.5% from March 2026 and up 4.9% from April 2025; nonstore retailers were up 11.1% year over year.
evidence.relevance: Supports ecommerce, marketplace, payments, and merchant-enablement demand nodes.

evidence.claim: Cached evidence: USDA ERS May 2026 Food Price Outlook reported April 2026 food-at-home CPI rose 0.7% month over month and 2.9% year over year, and forecast 2026 food-at-home prices to increase 3.2%.
evidence.relevance: Supports grocery, private-label, staples, value retail, egg/input-chain, and food-distribution candidates.

evidence.claim: Cached evidence: Census Q4 2025 e-commerce release estimated seasonally adjusted U.S. retail e-commerce sales of $316.1 billion and e-commerce at 16.6% of total retail sales in Q4 2025; full-year 2025 e-commerce was 16.4% of total retail sales.
evidence.relevance: Supports ecommerce platforms, merchant software, fulfillment automation, and retail-media nodes.

evidence.claim: Cached evidence: Walmart disclosed total eCommerce net sales grew $8.5 billion, or 26%, for the three months ended April 30, 2026, primarily driven by store and club-fulfilled delivery.
evidence.relevance: Supports fulfillment automation, last-mile/store-fulfilled delivery, grocery distribution infrastructure, and omnichannel retail nodes.
evidence.source_title: Walmart Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 30, 2026

evidence.claim: Cached evidence: Walmart disclosed Walmart U.S. comparable sales increased 4.3% for the three months ended April 30, 2026, driven by transactions and average ticket, with strength in grocery and general merchandise; U.S. eCommerce contributed about 5.2% to comparable sales.
evidence.relevance: Supports value retail, grocery, private-label, retail media, and omnichannel candidates; also raises the bar for weaker mass-retail competitors.
evidence.source_title: Walmart Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 30, 2026

evidence.claim: Cached evidence: Visa reported fiscal Q2 2026 net revenue growth of 17%, payments volume up 9% constant-dollar, cross-border volume up 12%, and processed transactions up 9%.
evidence.relevance: Supports broad payments, travel, cross-border, and consumer transaction rail demand; used as node evidence, not as a ranked candidate.
evidence.source_title: Visa Reports Fiscal Second Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: Cached evidence: The White House issued a February 20, 2026 proclamation imposing a temporary import surcharge with exceptions related to domestic supply availability, raw materials, supply dislocation avoidance, and goods in transit.
evidence.relevance: Supports risk assessment for imported consumer goods, retailers, private-label sourcing, closeout inventory, and margin volatility.
evidence.source_title: Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge to Address Fundamental International Payments Problems

evidence.claim: Cached evidence: The White House issued an April 2026 proclamation making Section 232 duties on aluminum, steel, and copper articles and derivative articles apply to the full customs value of imported products from April 6, 2026.
evidence.relevance: Supports tariff and input-cost risk checks for consumer goods, retail margins, and supply-chain candidates.
evidence.source_title: Strengthening Actions Taken to Adjust Imports of Aluminum, Steel, and Copper Into the United States

memory_update.content: For the Consumer theme, prioritize candidates with durable demand plus infrastructure/platform/control-point traits over undifferentiated discretionary retail beta.

Highest-priority nodes in this chunk: integrated marketplace-payments-logistics, consumer-credit underwriting infrastructure, merchant commerce rails, asset-light travel loyalty, grocery/private-label/retail-media frequency, and fulfillment automation.

Before promoting any Layer 3 candidate to a thesis, collect latest primary-source filings or earnings releases for company-specific revenue drivers, margin quality, customer concentration, regulatory/tariff exposure, and falsification metrics.

Travel and discretionary retail candidates require stronger macro and company-specific confirmation because fuel, airfare, credit stress, tariff costs, and middle-income consumer weakness can quickly invalidate demand assumptions.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest primary-source evidence on GMV growth, fintech TPV, credit quality, logistics penetration, advertising revenue, take-rate durability, and country-level macro/currency risks.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Highest-quality Serenity candidate in this chunk because it maps to multiple reinforcing consumer infrastructure nodes: ecommerce marketplace, payments, credit, logistics, and advertising in Latin America. The platform is less dependent on one U.S. retail-sales print and has potential bottleneck traits through fulfillment density, payments acceptance, merchant access, and data-driven credit rails.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current evidence on pricing power, lender adoption, mortgage/auto/card volume sensitivity, regulatory challenges, alternative-data competition, and whether revenue growth is volume-led or price-led.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Strong chokepoint candidate if consumer credit stress, underwriting precision, and lender risk controls become more important than headline consumption growth. Credit scoring has clearer supplier scarcity and infrastructure characteristics than most retailers or travel platforms in the chunk.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest primary evidence on GMV, merchant additions, payments penetration, attach rates, operating leverage, enterprise traction, AI commerce tooling, and competitive pressure from marketplaces and social commerce.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Commerce infrastructure exposure is cleaner than most discretionary consumer names. Shopify is tied to merchant enablement, checkout, payments, ecommerce tooling, and DTC brand formation. It benefits if ecommerce share continues rising, but the bottleneck is softer than true regulated or scarce-supplier nodes because merchants have other platform options.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest RevPAR by region, net unit growth, franchise fee growth, loyalty contribution, business versus leisure mix, and evidence that experience-led spend is not weakening.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Asset-light lodging and loyalty platform maps well to the travel-experiences node. Brand, loyalty, corporate relationships, and franchise scale provide some bottleneck qualities without heavy owned-asset exposure. It should be upgraded if RevPAR, net unit growth, loyalty engagement, and international travel remain resilient.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest company-specific evidence on identical sales, private-label penetration, retail-media growth, pharmacy/grocery margin, shrink, wage pressure, and competitive share versus Walmart, Costco, Aldi, and clubs.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: High-frequency grocery demand, private-label exposure, and shopper-data monetization make Kroger a strong Consumer theme candidate. The cached food-inflation evidence supports durable grocery/value demand, while retail media adds a higher-margin data layer. Bottleneck severity is moderate because grocery retail is competitive and supplier scarcity is limited.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest backlog, deployment cadence, customer concentration, gross margin, system acceptance timing, Walmart-related exposure, new-customer wins, and proof that automation demand is broadening beyond a few anchor accounts.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Second-order infrastructure candidate tied to retailer and grocer fulfillment automation. The cached Walmart evidence that ecommerce growth was driven primarily by store and club-fulfilled delivery supports the need for throughput, labor efficiency, and inventory accuracy. Symbotic has higher bottleneck potential than most retailers but needs customer concentration and deployment-risk checks.

ranked_candidates.company: Visa Inc. proxy evidence for payments node
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Excluded from ranked candidate set because ticker V is not in the candidate chunk.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Not part of the supplied candidate chunk and therefore excluded from ranking. Included here only as a node-level evidence anchor would violate the requested candidate-only constraint.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest segment disclosure on private-label exposure, volume versus price, input-cost pass-through, retailer concentration, capacity utilization, and category share in cereals, refrigerated, nut butters, pasta, and related staples.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Private-label and packaged-food manufacturing is a plausible second-order beneficiary if grocery inflation and trade-down behavior persist. Post has clearer supply-chain mapping than discretionary retailers, but its bottleneck status depends on category-level capacity, retailer relationships, and margin pass-through.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest nights and experiences booked, ADR trends, supply growth, urban regulation impact, cross-border recovery, take rate, repeat usage, and evidence that demand is not shifting back to hotels.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Alternative lodging marketplace is a clean public-market mapping to experience-led consumer spend and cross-border travel. The platform has network-effect characteristics, but regulatory risk and supply elasticity make the bottleneck less clean than credit rails, payments rails, or fulfillment automation.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest room-night growth, B2B growth, Vrbo performance, marketing efficiency, take rate, loyalty migration, direct-booking pressure, and AI/search disintermediation risk.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Expedia provides direct exposure to online travel demand, lodging marketplace economics, packaging, and travel advertising. It has platform characteristics, but supplier scarcity is moderate because travelers and hotels can route through competing OTAs, direct channels, search, and loyalty ecosystems.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current egg pricing, flock health, avian influenza impact, cage-free capacity, feed costs, retail contract mix, and whether profitability is structurally improving or simply price-cycle driven.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Eggs are a high-frequency staple with real supply constraints from flock capacity, avian influenza, feed costs, and cage-free regulation. This makes Cal-Maine a legitimate input-chain candidate, though its earnings can be highly cyclical and commodity-price-driven rather than a stable platform chokepoint.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest comparable sales, transaction versus ticket, new-store productivity, closeout deal flow, gross margin, inventory quality, and evidence that vendor supply remains favorable.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Extreme-value and closeout retail can benefit from both consumer trade-down and excess inventory created by retail disruption. Public-market purity is high, but supply access can be episodic; the thesis weakens if inventory availability normalizes or consumers rotate back to full-price discretionary channels.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest customer concentration, private-brand growth, distribution margin, leverage, contract renewals, working-capital pressure, and evidence that smaller grocers are gaining rather than losing share.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: UNFI maps to grocery distribution and private-brand enablement for smaller grocers. The node is strategically relevant if independents need scale to compete with mass merchants and clubs. However, supplier scarcity and pricing power appear weaker than platform, credit, or automation chokepoints.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest mortgage-volume sensitivity, Workforce Solutions growth, pricing, regulatory exposure, data-breach/legal risk, and whether consumer-credit demand is offsetting housing cyclicality.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Credit bureau and employment-data infrastructure is relevant if consumer underwriting and credit monitoring become more important. It has real data-scarcity traits, but consumer-theme purity is lower than FICO because business mix includes mortgage, workforce, and broader data services beyond direct consumer spend.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest comparable sales by category, traffic versus ticket, discretionary recovery, same-day fulfillment economics, retail-media growth, private-label margin, shrink, and tariff exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Target has relevant private-label, same-day fulfillment, grocery, discretionary, and retail-media exposure, but its Consumer theme quality is held back by middle-income discretionary sensitivity and weaker evidence of being a hard-to-replicate bottleneck versus Walmart, Costco, Kroger, or pure infrastructure names.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need latest delinquencies, net charge-offs, reserve build, card purchase volume, funding cost, deposit beta, acquisition/integration risk, and cohort-level credit performance.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Capital One is a useful consumer-stress and payments-volume monitor, but it is more of a cyclical credit-risk exposure than a clean Serenity chokepoint. It ranks lower because charge-offs, funding costs, and income-cohort stress can dominate any benefit from payment-volume resilience.

summary: Within this Consumer candidate chunk, the highest Serenity research priorities are the companies closest to durable consumer-demand infrastructure or harder-to-replicate supply-chain/control points: MercadoLibre for integrated LatAm marketplace-payments-logistics, Fair Isaac for consumer-credit underwriting infrastructure, Shopify for merchant commerce rails, Hilton for asset-light travel loyalty, and Kroger for grocery frequency plus private-label and retail-media data. Travel marketplaces and discretionary retailers remain relevant but rank lower where regulatory, cyclicality, or weak bottleneck evidence reduces chokepoint quality. This is research prioritization only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
